title: Eoduksini: Korea’s Darkness Figure, Names and Modern Retellings
metaDescription: Eoduksini is a darkness figure familiar from modern Korean storytelling. Language guidance uses Eodukseoni; a modern performance links its size to the attention it receives.
description: Eoduksini is a darkness figure familiar from modern Korean storytelling. Language guidance uses Eodukseoni; a modern performance links its size to the attention it receives.
storyHooks: A photographer earns a living by recording a growing shadow. When someone is trapped inside it, turning off the camera becomes a costly choice.

sections.origin: In a 2025 answer, the National Institute of Korean Language identifies 어둑서니 (Eodukseoni) as the standard form. It does not confirm the proposed etymology in the reader’s question.
sections.legend: The Asia Culture Center’s description of a children’s performance called Eoduksini presents a being that grows with attention and becomes smaller without it. This is a documented modern use of the motif.
sections.variants: A linguistic answer and a theatre synopsis answer different questions. Neither, by itself, verifies a claim that the creature was a guardian in the Goryeo period or that one method defeats it in every tradition.
sections.culture: When adapting the attention motif, identify the performance as a modern example. The Korean-language companion entry also discusses regional names and why a single bestiary category cannot settle every relationship between them.

sources.title: National Institute of Korean Language — answer dated 21 February 2025
Asia Culture Center — online theatre programme

researchNote: The sources establish language guidance and a modern performance, not an ancient origin narrative.

questions.question: Are Eoduksini and Eodukseoni the same spelling?
questions.answer: No. Eoduksini reflects 어둑시니; the language institute’s answer gives 어둑서니 as the standard Korean form.

questions.question: Is ignoring it an ancient rule?
questions.answer: This page verifies the attention motif in a modern performance description, not as a universal ancient rule.
